title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Earnestly Implementing the Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Jurisdiction of Administrative Cases
keywords_en: guarantee; administrative litigation; concerning administrative cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Earnestly Implementing the Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases

Fa Fa [2008] No. 7

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region

The Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases (Fa Shi [2008] No. 1, hereinafter referred to as the Jurisdiction Provisions) of the Supreme People's Court will come into force on February 1, 2008. To accurately grasp and correctly apply the Jurisdiction Provisions, the relevant issues are hereby notified as follows:

I. Fully recognize the significant importance of formulating and implementing the Jurisdiction Provisions

Since the promulgation and implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of China, people's courts at all levels have continuously attached importance to strengthening and actively carrying out administrative adjudication, achieving remarkable accomplishments and making important contributions to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations, supervising, supporting, and promoting law-based administration, and maintaining social harmony and stability. At the same time, it must be observed that factors currently affecting the development of administrative adjudication still exist to varying degrees, among which an unsatisfactory judicial environment remains a relatively prominent issue. The phenomenon of some local governments and administrative departments failing to understand, cooperate with, respect, or even interfering in the people's courts' acceptance and trial of administrative cases has not been well resolved, thereby affecting the exercise of independent and impartial judicial review by the people's courts and the functioning of administrative adjudication. The Party Central Committee and the State Council attach great importance to strengthening and improving administrative adjudication and have put forward clear requirements for actively and steadily advancing administrative litigation reform, exploring and perfecting reform measures for the jurisdictional system of administrative cases, and ensuring that the people's courts independently and impartially exercise their administrative adjudication functions in accordance with the law. The Jurisdiction Provisions constitute an important measure by the Supreme People's Court to deepen judicial system reform and have significant practical and far-reaching historical significance for further improving the judicial environment for administrative adjudication and ensuring that the people's courts independently and impartially hear administrative cases in accordance with the law. People's courts at all levels must deeply understand the important significance of formulating and implementing the Jurisdiction Provisions and earnestly implement them in judicial practice.

II. Several issues to be properly handled during implementation

First, take ensuring independent and impartial adjudication as the goal. The purpose of reforming the jurisdictional system for administrative cases is to prevent and eliminate improper interference, enabling the people's courts to independently and impartially accept and hear administrative cases. Therefore, in determining the jurisdiction of a case, the standard must be whether it facilitates the independent and impartial adjudication by the people's court. For cases where there may be circumstances affecting the independence and impartiality of adjudication, the lower-level people's court shall proactively report to the higher-level people's court for jurisdiction or designated jurisdiction, and the higher-level people's court shall, in accordance with the Jurisdiction Provisions, promptly make a decision on designated jurisdiction or elevating the level of jurisdiction.

Second, combine the initiation by the litigant with the decision by the people's court. The Jurisdiction Provisions grant litigants a certain degree of choice in initiating designated jurisdiction or elevating the level of jurisdiction, but the final decision on whether to implement designated jurisdiction or elevate the level of jurisdiction must be made by the people's court. If a citizen, legal person, or other organization considers a case to be major or complex or believes that the basic people's court with jurisdiction is not suitable to exercise jurisdiction, they may directly file a lawsuit with the intermediate people's court. In response to such a lawsuit, the intermediate people's court shall determine the jurisdiction based on local actual conditions and the specific circumstances of the case. If there are grounds that may affect fair adjudication, it shall designate another basic people's court within its jurisdiction to hear the case or decide to hear it itself; if it considers that the people's court at the location of the defendant can ensure the fairness and efficiency of the case trial, it may also notify the plaintiff in writing to file a lawsuit with the basic people's court that has jurisdiction.

Third, focus on designated jurisdiction, supplemented by elevating the level of jurisdiction. Practice has proven that appropriately raising the trial level of certain individual administrative cases is necessary to ensure fair trial, while also adhering to and reflecting the principle and spirit of resolving contradictions and disputes at the grassroots level. While making appropriate adjustments to the first-instance administrative cases under the jurisdiction of intermediate people's courts, the Jurisdiction Provisions focus on stipulations concerning designated jurisdiction by intermediate people's courts. In implementation, all localities shall adhere to designated jurisdiction as the primary method, resorting to elevating the level of jurisdiction only when truly necessary, so as to resolve administrative disputes at the grassroots level as much as possible.

Fourth, balance convenience for litigation with case load equilibrium. Designated jurisdiction may cause a certain degree of inconvenience to litigants. Therefore, when determining the court of jurisdiction, the principle of proximity should be adopted as much as possible. In remote areas with inconvenient transportation, the difficulties and burdens of litigants should be considered, and where necessary, the opinions of the litigants may be solicited. At the same time, attention should be paid to appropriately balancing the workload of basic people's courts in hearing administrative cases through designated jurisdiction, so as to achieve a reasonable allocation of judicial resources.

Fifth, prevent fixed corresponding jurisdiction between courts. When designating a court of jurisdiction, the intermediate people's court should, as far as possible, avoid forming a regular fixed corresponding jurisdiction between two people's courts, to prevent negative effects arising therefrom that may affect the role of designated jurisdiction.

Sixth, coordinate and cooperate between the case-filing division and the adjudication division. Issues concerning the acceptance and jurisdiction of administrative cases are often relatively complex. Given that the administrative adjudication division is more familiar with the scope of acceptance and the requirements for filing, and has a better understanding of the judicial environment, the quality of administrative cases, and the allocation of administrative adjudication personnel in courts within its jurisdiction, when deciding on jurisdictional issues, the case-filing division and the administrative adjudication division shall strengthen communication and coordination. The case-filing division shall actively seek the opinions of the administrative adjudication division before making a decision on how to determine the court of jurisdiction. High people's courts and intermediate people's courts shall, in light of local actual conditions, formulate corresponding specific measures concerning the division of labor and connection for the jurisdictional work of administrative cases.

Seventh, focus on improving and optimizing the grassroots judicial environment. In practice, grassroots people's courts are relatively more subject to interference in administrative adjudication. The Jurisdiction Provisions focus on stipulating designated jurisdiction and jurisdiction by level for first-instance administrative cases under the jurisdiction of basic people's courts. For first-instance administrative cases under the jurisdiction of intermediate people's courts and high people's courts, if they need to be tried by the higher-level people's court or subject to designated jurisdiction, reference may be made to these Provisions.

Eighth, standardize and unify judicial documents related to case jurisdiction. The implementation of the Jurisdiction Provisions involves the preparation of relevant judicial documents. To standardize and unify judicial documents related to case jurisdiction, attached to this Notice are sample judicial documents for administrative case jurisdiction for trial use by people's courts at all levels. If problems arise during the trial, promptly report them to our court.

III. Earnestly implement the Jurisdiction Provisions

Although the Jurisdiction Provisions contain only a few articles, their reform of the administrative litigation system is substantial, and the resulting social impact will be far-reaching. People's courts at all levels must fully understand and grasp the essential spirit and significant importance of the Jurisdiction Provisions, adjust work approaches, rationalize working mechanisms, improve relevant work systems, and strengthen the leadership and guidance in implementing this judicial interpretation. All case-filing and administrative adjudication personnel shall be organized to study each article, accurately understand, and strictly grasp the spirit and requirements of the Jurisdiction Provisions and this Notice. When necessary, publicity activities may be organized within a certain scope to enhance understanding and support from the people and all sectors of society. High people's courts and intermediate people's courts shall strengthen research and guidance to lower-level courts, formulate implementation plans in light of local actual conditions, and promptly report new situations and problems arising during implementation to the higher-level court.

This notice is hereby given.

January 14, 2008
